body.value: These three customers — keys 208369, 556838 and 595495 — are the only people on Contoso's register who placed at least one order in every calendar quarter of 2025, and the 4 beside each is the number of distinct 2025 quarters they bought in. For scale: of the 13,834 customers who bought anything in 2025, 12,553 appeared in only one quarter, 1,219 in two, 59 in three, and these 3 in all four. What the figure does NOT include: nothing about how much they spent, how many orders they placed, or what they bought — the test is merely presence in a quarter, so one small order per quarter counts the same as fifty. It does not say which quarters, because all four is the only qualifying pattern. And it hands back keys rather than names, which is as close to "which customers" as the suppression on customer_name allows.

value: a list of names and figures

The 13,834 customer accounts that placed at least one order with an order_date in calendar 2025 — 3 of them qualified. Restrictions I applied, and where each came from: (1) the period read on `order_date`, not `delivery_date`, because order.default.period_is_order_date declares `default: ordered`; I measured the alternative and it returns the same three customers. (2) Calendar quarters, because this bundle declares no fiscal calendar, so fiscal quarters cannot be computed at all. (3) BOTH sales channels — shop and web shop — with no channel predicate, because store.resolution.the_channel_is_the_location_sentinel is scoped `applies: subject` and the subject here is customers, not stores (operator's ruling of 2026-10-18). (4) One row per individual customer account, no roll-up to household or parent company, as no such column is declared. (5) Every recorded purchase line counted, with no exclusion for cancellations or returns: the fact declares no status, cancellation or return column, and the lowest quantity anywhere is 1 and the lowest net amount 0.83, so there is no reversing line to exclude. The three are identified by `customer_key`, not by name, because dim_customer.customer_name is declared SUPPRESSED (DQ-IDENTIFYING-DIM_CUSTOMER-CUSTOMER_NAME). Excluded by the question's own terms: the 38,355 registered customers who bought in an earlier year but not in 2025, and the 52,801 who have never bought anything.

One row is one product on one order by one customer on one day in 2025. The distinct-customer count for the year is deliberately not stated here: the per-quarter figures (3,931 / 3,096 / 3,693 / 4,460) cannot be added, because a customer who bought in two quarters appears in both — that count arrives at the grouping step. 2025 is a complete year in this bundle: the newest order anywhere is 2025-12-31, so Q4 is not a part-quarter.

The declared default settles the choice, but because the final answer is an all-four-quarters membership test rather than a sum, a handful of boundary orders could still move individual customers in or out — so I will report the final customer count under both readings

WITH by_order AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    COUNT(DISTINCT QUARTER(order_date)) AS quarters
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  WHERE
    YEAR(order_date) = 2025
  GROUP BY
    customer_key
), by_delivery AS (
  SELECT
    customer_key,
    COUNT(DISTINCT QUARTER(delivery_date)) AS quarters
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  WHERE
    YEAR(delivery_date) = 2025
  GROUP BY
    customer_key
)
SELECT
  'ordered' AS reading,
  quarters AS quarters_of_2025_bought_in,
  COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM by_order
GROUP BY
  1,
  2
UNION ALL
SELECT
  'delivered' AS reading,
  quarters AS quarters_of_2025_bought_in,
  COUNT(*) AS customers
FROM by_delivery
GROUP BY
  1,
  2
ORDER BY
  reading DESC,
  quarters_of_2025_bought_in

  SELECT
    customer_key
  FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line
  WHERE
    YEAR(order_date) = 2025

  HAVING

  WHERE
    YEAR(delivery_date) = 2025
  GROUP BY
    customer_key
  HAVING
    COUNT(DISTINCT QUARTER(delivery_date)) = 4
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(o.customer_key, d.customer_key) AS customer_key,
  (
    NOT o.customer_key IS NULL
  ) AS qualifies_on_order_date,
  (
    NOT d.customer_key IS NULL
  ) AS qualifies_on_delivery_date
FROM by_order AS o
FULL OUTER JOIN by_delivery AS d
  ON o.customer_key = d.customer_key
ORDER BY
  customer_key
